polycube.context: Three equal cubes joined face to face into an L-shaped block, drawn in 3D. Used for combinatorics and puzzle topics, voxel and block building, and 3D geometry lessons.

annular-sector.context: A curved block cut from a ring, bounded by two arcs and two straight ends, with the rest of the ring dashed. Used in geometry lessons on area of a ring segment, and for arch stones, gauges and donut chart slices.

extrude.context: A hexagonal prism rising from a flat face with an arrow pointing up out of its top. Used in 3D modelling and CAD software for the extrude or push pull tool.

polyline.context: An open zigzag chain of straight segments with a marked point at every joint and both ends. Used for polyline and path drawing tools in design, mapping and CAD apps, and for polygonal chains in geometry.

pyramid-frustum.context: A square pyramid with its top sliced off flat, leaving a smaller square top face. Used in geometry and volume lessons, and for truncated pyramid shapes in architecture and packaging.

parabolic-focus.context: Two parallel rays coming down onto a parabola and bouncing off it to meet at the focus point. Used for reflector optics, satellite dishes, solar cookers and parabola lessons.

vector-projection.context: Two arrows from one start point, with a dashed line dropped at a right angle from one tip onto the other. Used in linear algebra and physics for projections, components and the dot product.

miura-fold.context: A sheet creased into a zigzag grid of slanted parallelograms, the pattern of a Miura fold. Used for origami, folding maps, deployable solar panels and engineering design topics.

hollow-cylinder.context: An upright tube whose top face is a ring between an outer and an inner circle. Used for pipes, tubes, bushings and rings, and in geometry lessons on the volume of a hollow cylinder.

quadtree.context: A square split into four quarters, with one quarter split into four again and points in the larger cells. Used for spatial indexing, image compression, maps and collision detection in games.

unit-cell.context: A wireframe cube with an atom at each of its eight corners, the repeating block of a crystal lattice. Used in chemistry, materials science and crystallography.

oblique-cone.context: A cone whose tip leans to one side, not straight above the centre of its round base, with a dashed axis. Used in geometry lessons on slanted solids and volume.

oblique-cylinder.context: A cylinder whose top is shifted sideways from its base so the sides lean, with the hidden back of the base dashed. Used in geometry lessons on slanted solids and volume.

cyclic-quadrilateral.context: A four-sided shape drawn inside a circle with all four corners on the circle. Used in geometry lessons on inscribed shapes, circle theorems and opposite angles.

triangle-midsegment.context: A triangle with a line joining the midpoints of two sides, parallel to the base, with both midpoints marked. Used in geometry lessons on the midsegment theorem and similar triangles.

cube-space-diagonal.context: A see-through cube with a line running from one corner through the inside to the opposite corner. Used in geometry lessons on space diagonals, 3D distance and the Pythagorean theorem in three dimensions.

folium-of-descartes.context: A curve with a leaf-shaped loop at the top whose two tails spread out and run toward a dashed straight line. Used in calculus and algebra lessons on implicit curves and asymptotes.

zollner-illusion.context: Three parallel lines crossed by short slanted hatch marks that alternate direction from line to line, which makes the lines look tilted. Used in psychology and vision science to show optical illusions.

sander-illusion.context: A parallelogram split into a big and a small part, each crossed by a diagonal; the two diagonals are equal in length but look different. Used in psychology and vision science to show optical illusions.

spherical-wedge.context: A slice cut from a ball like an orange segment, showing its curved skin and one flat half-disc face. Used in geometry lessons on sphere volume and in 3D modelling.

truncated-hexagonal-tiling.context: A square patch of a tiling in which large twelve-sided tiles meet with a small triangle filling the gap at each corner where three tiles touch. Used for tessellation and pattern studies, crystal and lattice diagrams, floor tile and game map layouts, and geometry lessons on semiregular tilings.
